description: Ω5 provider (v0.2.0 — Ω10/Ω11b: appends message.receive@1, the inbound-ingest simulator) — file-backed email over the user's vault. Implements the six message.* contracts DECLARED by pack.domain-email (same ids/versions — cross-plugin contract implementation is the PREFERRED state, not a conflict): messages persist as vault objects in ns 'email' via port calls (data/code divorce — this plugin owns no storage), so replacing the provider keeps the data.

provider.doc: send {to, subject, body, threadId?} → vault.append@1 (ns email, meta.type message) → {messageId, rev, sentAt}. Risk/risk-class for this op is DECLARED by pack.domain-email (risk lives on contract kind only).
list {folder?, limit?} → vault.query@1 + bounded vault.get@1 → summaries (no bodies).
read {id} → full message; sets flags.seen via a separate vault.append revision (the op contract is READ; the internal append is provider-side, gated as vault.append@1 MUTATION).
move {id, folder} → appends a new revision with the folder changed.

receive {from, subject, body, folder?} → ONE vault.append@1 (ns email, meta.type message) → {messageId, rev, receivedAt, folder}. The message lands in folder inbox (default), to = the configured self address, flags unseen. READ by pack declaration: ingestion is vault-internal. SIMULATOR SEMANTICS (documented per D-222): the real leg of this contract is an IMAP provider polling an external mailbox; this file provider simulates the inbound leg by ingesting the message directly — the vault state (and the director's rule loop watching ns 'email') is identical, so 'when Peter messages me' rules fire the same way in simulation and in production.

capabilities.justification: Messages persist in the USER'S VAULT, not in this plugin (data/code divorce): appending a message/flag/folder revision needs port:vault.append@1; list/search/read need port:vault.get@1, port:vault.query@1, port:vault.search@1. The composition grants exactly these four per user-signed Recipe — never this manifest.
